Action.description:
The action of a rule (#34).

Each action is an object with a `type`, and its options as optional
keys, so options can be added later without a breaking change.

oneOf.description: Permit execution.
Block execution.

allow_request.description:
The end user may raise an approval request (#11). Needs a
notification, and is not valid in a mandatory rule set.

kill_running.description:
Terminate already-running instances that match when the policy is
applied. Not valid for drivers or libraries.

on_unparseable.description:
Whether a version fact that is not a version counts towards the
rule applying (#32, #35). With `match`, each version criterion on
such a fact is taken in whichever direction makes the deny apply,
also under `not`. The rest of the tree is evaluated as usual.
`no_match`, the default, leaves the criterion `Unknown`, which
`unknown_as` then decides.

request_template.description: The approval request template to use. Only with `allow_request`.

unknown_as.description:
Whether the rule blocks when its match tree is `Unknown` because a
fact is missing or cannot be trusted (#32, #35). `no_match`, the
default, means an unknown fact does not block; `match` makes the
deny fail closed.

oneOf.description:
Record the match without changing the outcome. A non-terminal
annotation, used for detection and tagging.

Permit execution inside a containment profile (#14). The engine only
carries the reference.

profile_id.description: The containment profile the process runs under.

oneOf.description:
Permit execution with an elevated token (#12). The engine only
carries the directive.

auth.description: What the user must do to confirm.

reason_prompt.description:
If set, the user must give a reason, and this is the prompt shown:
one line of 1 to 256 characters, trimmed, with no control characters
(including tab and line breaks) and no bidirectional formatting
characters, so the prompt cannot be made to read differently.

token_profile.description: The access token profile to build the token from.

oneOf.description:
Mark the matching process as a trusted installer, updater or source
(#9, #114). This does not permit the process itself to run; an allow
rule decides that. The engine returns the directive.

scope_paths.description:
The folders whose new content becomes trusted: 1 to 32 absolute paths
(`C:\...`, `\\server\share\...`, or a known path variable such as
`%PROGRAMFILES%\...`), each at most 1024 bytes, written with `\`, and
unique (compared as the engine compares paths).

tag_output.description:
Tag the files written with a persistent trust claim, so they stay
trusted after the process exits. Off by default.

oneOf.description:
Skip the object entirely: no decision is logged. Only for performance
exclusions, never for executables or drivers, and validation always
warns.
No opinion. A first-match model continues with the next rule (#35).

anyOf.description: A string of at most 2048 bytes, with no control characters.

AllowTiebreak.description: Which allow decides among allows of different kinds.

oneOf.description:
`allow_contained`, then `allow`, then `allow_elevated` (with
`condition: always` before `if_required`). The default.

The reverse: `allow_elevated` (`if_required` before `always`), then
`allow`, then `allow_contained`.

ApprovalScope.description: Who a device-local approval applies to.

oneOf.description: Only the user who approved it. The default.
Every user of the device.

Cadence.description:
When the agent refreshes a probed fact (#33, #329). The result is cached
in the context until then.

oneOf.description: Once in each logon session.
Once after each boot.
Each time a new policy is applied.

ClientFilter.description:
The client connected to a remote desktop session, for per-client
scoping on multi-session hosts. Each list that is set must match.

device_sets.description: Device sets (#37) the client device is in.

hostname.description: Wildcards on the client's host name.

ip.description:
Address blocks (`10.0.0.0/8`) or ranges (`10.0.0.1-10.0.0.9`) for
the client's address.

CloudObject.description: An object in a cloud directory: a group of users or of devices.

oneOf.description: Every dimension that is set must match. The default.
At least one dimension that is set must match.

CompliancePreset.description:
A compliance preset: a named starting configuration. Changes that make
the policy weaker than its preset raise a compliance warning (#17).
Ordered from the least to the most demanding.

oneOf.description:
Essential Eight maturity level 1: block in user profiles, temporary
folders and other user-writable locations, detect elsewhere
(ISM-1870).

Essential Eight maturity level 2: block in every location
(ISM-1871).

Essential Eight maturity level 3: level 2, drivers blocked, and a
mandatory blocklist required (ISM-1658). Drivers loaded during early
boot are only audited unless `driver_boot_policy` is `enforce`;
validation warns about that exemption.

ContainmentProfileRef.description: The ID of a containment profile (#14, #173).

ControlLevel.description: Whether a class of object is controlled.

oneOf.description: Not evaluated.
Evaluated, and would-block decisions are reported only.
Evaluated and enforced.

Criterion.description:
A test of one fact about the object or its context: `field operator
values`.

Values are combined with OR for positive operators and with AND for
negative ones (#32): `not_contains [a, b]` means neither `a` nor `b`.

anchored.description:
Only for `regex` and `not_regex`: `false` lets the pattern match
anywhere in the fact instead of the whole fact (#32). Unset means
`true`.

arg_index.description:
Only for `process.argv`: the argument tested, from the start (0 is
the program name) or, when negative, from the end (-1 is the last).
Unset means any argument after the program name.

case_sensitive.description:
Compare strings case-sensitively. Unset means the field's default
(#32), which is case-insensitive for every field defined so far.
Only text, paths, file names, account names and tags have a case;
other fields (hashes, versions, SIDs, group sets, yes-or-no facts and
session types) reject this option.

evaluate.description:
When the agent refreshes what this criterion probes (#33, #329).
Required on a `cold` field (`fs.*`), allowed on a `warm` one
(`env.*`, `reg.*`), and not applicable to a `hot` one. Unset on a
warm field means every decision.

include_sub_ous.description:
Only for `user.ou` and `device.ou`: `true` also matches objects in
every organisational unit below the named one (#33). Unset means
`false`: the object must be directly in it.

match_ads.description:
Only for positive tests of `path.full`: `true` lets a value that
names no alternate data stream also match a stream of a file it
matches, so `C:\\Tools\\*` matches `C:\\Tools\\a.exe:s` (#32).
Unset means `false`: a stream is its own object.

safety_critical.description:
Only in a mandatory blocklist: when the fact is unknown, this
criterion counts towards the deny applying (`match`, or `no_match`
under an odd number of `not` nodes), so the shipped blocklists fail
closed (#32, #87). Unset means `false`.

set.description:
Only for `member_of` and `not_member_of` on a SHA-256 hash field
(`hash.sha256`, `hash.authenticode_sha256`, `hash.page_sha256`,
`hash.msi_fuzzy_sha256`): the library hash set the fact is tested
against (#368), by ID and pinned version, instead of `values`. The
hierarchy pins `latest` to the version it resolves; a bundle carries
the set itself. A set the evaluator does not have at that version,
for that field, is unknown, so it never lets an allow match.

signer.description:
Only for `signer.*` fields: which signatures take part, and what
each must also satisfy (#31). The options bind to the signature the
field is read from, so `min_key_bits` on a publisher test needs the
publisher's own signature to have the key size. Unset means every
option's default.

target.description:
Only for `env.*`, `reg.*` and `fs.*` fields, which need it: what the
criterion probes (#329). An environment variable's name; a registry
key, starting with its hive (`HKLM`, `HKCU`, `HKU` or `HKCR`, or
the long names); or a drive or UNC path, with no wildcard or stream.

value_name.description:
Only for `reg.value`: the name of the value. Unset means the key's
default value.

values.description:
1 to 25 values. Each is at most 2048 bytes of UTF-8; the schema can
only bound the length in characters, so validation checks the bytes.
`is_true` and `is_false` take no values, and the key may be left out.

DateRange.description: An inclusive range of dates. `to` unset means the single day `from`.

to.description: The last day, on or after `from`.

DeviceRef.description: A device or group of devices (#38).

oneOf.description: The device's Palisade ID.

A wildcard on the host name or the fully qualified domain name,
such as `FIN-*`. Case-insensitive.

A device set from the library (#37), static or dynamic. The server
works out which sets a device is in.
A directory computer group, by SID.
A cloud-directory device group.
A directory organisational unit.
A device tag, such as `site=sydney`. Case-insensitive.

DigestAlgorithm.description: A digest algorithm a signature uses (#31, ADR 0008).

oneOf.description: MD2.
MD5.
SHA-1.

name.description: The display name, for people. Never matched.

DriverBootPolicy.description:
How unknown drivers are handled while the device boots, before the agent
has fully started (`boot_phase: early`).

oneOf.description:
Report what would be blocked, and block nothing. The default, until
the tenant enables enforcement explicitly.
Apply the unknown-handling level.

Effects.description: The effect flags of one rule. Unset fields take the action's default.

help_url.description:
A link shown with the notification: an `https` URL of at most 2048
bytes. Only allowed when a notification is shown.

log.description:
Whether the decision produces a local event. `deny`, `audit`,
`allow_elevated` and `trust_source` need an event per decision, so
`summary` and `never` are not allowed on them.

notification_text.description:
The text of a `custom` notification: at most 2048 characters, with
the placeholders `{file}`, `{publisher}`, `{rule}`, `{user}` and
`{hash}`. Write `{{` and `}}` for literal braces. Required with
`notify: custom`, and only allowed with it.

notify.description: Whether the user is shown a notification.

severity.description: How serious the event is, for alerting (#16).

suppress_duplicates_secs.description:
The local de-duplication window, in seconds, at most 604800. `0`
turns de-duplication off. Detection counters still count every
occurrence.

tags.description:
Labels copied into the event, such as `lolbin` or
`mitre:T1218.005`: each 1 to 128 characters, at most 64.

upload.description: When the event is sent to the server.

ElevationAuth.description: The confirmation an `allow_elevated` action asks for.

oneOf.description: No confirmation. The default.
The user authenticates again.
The user completes a multi-factor challenge.
Every time the object runs.
Only when the object asks for administrator rights.

EnforcementOverride.description: How one rule relates to the policy mode (#36).

oneOf.description: Follow the effective mode. The default.
Enforce this rule even in audit or learning mode.
Never enforce this rule: it only reports what it would block.
Informational.
Low.
Medium.
High.
Critical.

Field.description:
The identity facts a criterion can test (#31).

This is the part of the #31 catalogue that has a matcher: hashes, the
signer and its certificates, the path and the version resource. The
other families (packaged apps, installers, ownership, origin and process
relationships) arrive in later minor versions, each with its facts and
matcher.

oneOf.description: SHA-256 of the whole file. The primary identity (ADR 0008).
SHA-384 of the whole file.
SHA-512 of the whole file.

SHA-256 Authenticode image hash: the PE image without its checksum,
security directory entry and certificate table.
SHA-1 Authenticode image hash. Compatibility only (ADR 0008).

SHA-256 hash of the first page of the image, for OS-native policy
formats. It covers only that page, so it is a weak identity alone.

SHA-1 hash of the first page of the image. Compatibility only
(ADR 0008).

SHA-256 of an installer package with its timestamps left out, so
rebuilds of the same content share one value (#3).
SHA-1 of the whole file. Compatibility only (ADR 0008).
MD5 of the whole file. Compatibility only (ADR 0008).
The leaf signer's subject common name.
The common name of the leaf certificate's issuer.
The SHA-256 thumbprint of the leaf certificate.
The normalised full path.
The parent directory.
The on-disk file name.
The file extension, without its leading dot.
The original file name from the version resource.
The internal name from the version resource.
The file description from the version resource.
The product name from the version resource.
The company name from the version resource.
The file version from the version resource.
The product version from the version resource.
Context (#33): the SID of the user the process runs as.

Context (#33): the user's account name, as `DOMAIN\user` or as a
user principal name (`user@example.org`). Either form can match.
Regular expressions are not allowed: match principals by SID where
you can (#32).

Context (#33): the groups in the user's token, as SIDs, and the
user's cloud-directory groups, as object IDs.
Context (#33): the SID of the user's primary group.

Context (#33): the token holds the local Administrators group,
enabled or filtered by UAC.
Context (#33): the token is elevated.
Context (#33): the user is a service account.
Context (#33): the user is the local system account.
Context (#33): the device's host name.
Context (#33): the device's fully qualified domain name.
Context (#33): the DNS name of the device's domain.
Context (#33): the device's NetBIOS name.
Context (#33): the directory site the device is in.

Context (#33): the device's computer groups, as SIDs, and its
cloud-directory device groups, as object IDs.
Context (#33): the Palisade tags assigned to the device.
Context (#33): the operating system version.
Context (#33): the operating system edition.
Context (#33): the processor architecture, such as `x64` or `arm64`.
Context (#33): the device runs a server edition.
Context (#33): the device is a domain controller.
Context (#33): the device is a laptop.
Context (#33): the device is a virtual desktop.
Context (#33): the device is a multi-session terminal server.

Context (#33): how the session was started: `console`, `rdp`,
`remote_shell`, `service`, `batch` or `network`.

Context (#33): the host name of the client connected to the session,
on a multi-session host.
Context (#33): the session is remote.

Context (#33): the integrity level of the process token: `untrusted`,
`low`, `medium`, `medium_plus`, `high`, `system` or `protected`.
Ordered, so `ge` and `le` compare levels.

Context (#33): the organisational unit of the user's directory
object, as a distinguished name such as `OU=Finance,DC=corp,DC=example`.
With `include_sub_ous`, units below it match too.

Context (#33): the organisational unit of the device's directory
object, as for `user.ou`.
Context (#33): the operating system build number, such as `22631`.
Context (#33): the session ID.

Context (#33): the IP address of the client connected to the
session, on a multi-session host.

Context (#33): every local interface address. A network test
(`ip_in_cidr`, `ip_between`, `ip_wildcard`) matches if any address
does; a set test holds the addresses as a set, so `all_of` needs
every listed address to be present.
Context (#33): every local interface MAC address.
Context (#33): every connection-specific DNS suffix.
Context (#33): the device can reach its server now.

Context (#33, #38): the names of the network locations the device is
in, such as `corporate`, `remote` or `offline`.

Context (#33): the day of the week of the evaluation, as `mon` to
`sun`, in the clock the policy's `time_zone_basis` names.

Context (#33): the time of day of the evaluation, as `HH:MM`, in the
policy's clock.

Context (#33): the date of the evaluation, as `YYYY-MM-DD`, in the
policy's clock.

The SHA-1 thumbprint of the leaf certificate. Compatibility only
(ADR 0008).

The subject common name of the highest certificate below the root,
as the signature provides it: the PCA.
The SHA-256 thumbprint of the chain's root certificate.

The SHA-1 thumbprint of the chain's root certificate. Compatibility
only (ADR 0008).

The hash of a chain certificate's `tbsCertificate`, under the
certificate's own signature digest (40, 64, 96 or 128 hex digits).
It identifies that one certificate: the `tbsCertificate` includes
the serial number and the validity period (RFC 5280), so a
certificate reissued with the same key has another TBS hash, and
each issue needs its own rule; `signer.spki_sha256` names the key
across every certificate that carries it. `signer.position` says
which certificate. A 40-digit (SHA-1) value is compatibility only
(ADR 0008).

The extended key usages of the leaf certificate, as dotted OIDs,
such as `1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.3` (code signing). A leaf without the
extension has none.

The SHA-256 of a chain certificate's DER `SubjectPublicKeyInfo`: its
public key (#318). Unlike the TBS hash it stays the same when a
certificate is reissued for the same key, so a deny on a stolen
key's hash also blocks every reissue. `signer.position` says which
certificate. A key above the leaf belongs to a certificate
authority, which vouches for everything it signs.
The `LegalCopyright` string from the version resource (#328).

The language and code page of the version-resource block the other
`meta.*` strings were read from, as its key is written: eight hex
digits, such as `040904b0` (#328).

The file's effective name (#328): the first of the original file
name, internal name, file description and product name that the
version resource has, or the name on disk when it has none.
The file's size in bytes, as a whole number (#328).

The PE image's COFF machine, by name: `i386`, `amd64`, `arm64`,
`arm64_ec`, `arm64_x`, `arm_nt` and so on (#328).

The PE image's subsystem, by name: `windows_gui`, `windows_cui`,
`native`, `efi_application` and so on (#328).

Whether the PE image is a .NET assembly: it has a CLR runtime header
(#328).

A Windows Installer package's `ProductCode` (#328), a GUID. Compared
as a GUID: braces and case do not matter.

A Windows Installer package's `UpgradeCode` (#328), a GUID shared by
every version of a product.

A Windows Installer package's `ProductName` (#328). Free text the
author chooses.

A Windows Installer package's `Manufacturer` (#328). Free text the
author chooses: never a publisher.
A Windows Installer package's `ProductVersion` (#328).

A Windows Installer package's `PackageCode` (#328): the GUID of one
build of the package.

The drive type of the file's volume, as the OS reports it (#328):
`fixed`, `removable`, `network`, `cd_rom` or `ram_disk`. An
`unknown` drive type is a missing fact.

The bus of the disk the file's volume is on (#328): `usb`, `sata`,
`nvme`, `scsi`, `sd`, `virtual`, `file_backed_virtual`, `iscsi` and
so on. An `unknown` bus is a missing fact.

Whether the file is on a network share: its path, or the other form
of it (a mapped drive's UNC path), is a UNC path (#328).
Whether the object is an alternate data stream of a file (#328).

The `\\server\share` a file on a network share is under (#328),
from its UNC path. A file on no share has none, so `equals` does not
match it.

Whether some non-administrator may change the permissions or the
owner of the file or a directory above it (#328).

What the file's content is, from its bytes (#30, #328): `pe`,
`msi`, `script`, `zip`, `lnk`, `text` and so on, in
`palisade-fileid`'s names. `unknown` is a missing fact.

What the file's name claims it is, from its extension (#30, #328):
one of the [`Self::MetaDetectedType`] names, or `none` (no
extension), `inert` (a document or media extension) or `other`. A
PE renamed to `.pdf` has `meta.detected_type` `pe` and
`meta.extension_type` `inert`.

Context (#329): the value of the environment variable `target` in
the process's environment block. User-controlled: a user sets their
own environment, so it can only narrow a rule.

Context (#329): whether the registry key `target` exists, such as
`HKLM\\Software\\Vendor\\App`. Keys under `HKCU`, `HKU` and
`HKCR` are user-controlled.

Context (#329): the registry value `value_name` (unset: the key's
default value) of the key `target`. A `REG_DWORD` or `REG_QWORD` is
a number, which `eq` to `between` compare; text is compared as
text. Values under `HKCU`, `HKU` and `HKCR` are user-controlled.

Context (#329): whether the file `target` exists. User-controlled:
whether a user can create or remove a file depends on where it is,
which a policy cannot see, so every file-system test is treated as
one a user may control (ADR 0018).

Context (#329): whether the folder `target` exists. User-controlled,
as `fs.file`.

Context (#329): the command line the process was started with, as
the agent captured it at creation. Attacker-controlled: whoever
starts a process chooses its arguments, so it can only narrow a
rule.

Context (#329): the process's arguments, split as
`CommandLineToArgvW` splits them. With `arg_index`, the argument at
that position (0 is the program name, -1 the last); without it, any
argument after the program name. Attacker-controlled, as
`process.command_line`.

FindingSeverity.description: How serious a policy-assistant finding is (#40).

oneOf.description: Informational.
Probably a mistake or a risk.
Blocks publishing unless a tenant administrator overrides it.

GovernanceSettings.description: The tenant's governance settings (#40). Every field is optional.

counter_report_hours.description:
How often the agent reports hit counters, in hours: 1 to 168,
default 24.

expiring_soon_days.description:
A rule that expires within this many days is expiring soon: 1 to
365, default 14.

expiry_notice_days.description:
When the server tells a rule's owner that it expires, in days
before the expiry: at most 8 values, each at most 365, default
`[14, 3, 0]`.

require_justification.description:
Governance mode: allow, trust, exclusion and exception rules need a
justification, allow and trust rules a review date, and exception
rules an expiry, an approver and a risk rating. Unset means on for
a policy with a compliance preset (`unknown.preset`) and off
otherwise.

severity.description:
The severity of policy-assistant findings, per finding code,
replacing the default.

stale_after_days.description:
A rule with no hits for this many days, while usage was observed,
is stale: 1 to 3650, default 90.

Level.description:
How an unknown object is handled. The variants are declared from least
to most restrictive, so `Ord` is the restrictiveness order.

oneOf.description:
Allowed silently. Validation warns, and Essential Eight presets do
not permit it for user profiles or temporary folders.
Allowed, but logged with severity medium and flagged unhandled.

The user is asked (#11). Not for libraries, drivers, objects that a
blocklist matched, or sessions with no interactive user; those get
the prompt's fallback.

Allowed inside the `restrict_profile` containment profile (#14).
Only for executables, scripts and installers. It fails closed to
`block` when the containment component is not installed.
Blocked. The default.

LibraryId.description: A UUID version 7 in canonical lowercase form.

LibraryRef.description: A reference to a library from a match tree or a hierarchy assignment.

pin.description: The version: `latest` (the default) or a version number.

LocationProfile.description:
A named network location, such as `corporate`: every test must match
(#38). The agent evaluates the profiles when the network changes and on
every heartbeat, and scopes test the result with `location_profile`.

all.description: The tests, all of which must match. No `location_profile` tests.

name.description:
The profile's name: 1 to 64 characters, letters, digits, `_`, `.`
or `-`. Compared without case.

LogLevel.description: Whether a decision produces a local event.

oneOf.description: Every decision produces an event.

Decisions are aggregated into periodic summaries per device, user,
object and rule. The default for allow rules.
A sample of decisions produces events.
No event.

Match.description:
A condition tree (#33).

Each node is an object with exactly one key: `all`, `any`, `not`,
`criterion` or `ref`.

oneOf.description:
Matches when every child matches. Needs at least one child, except
as the whole match of a `catch_all` rule, where an empty `all`
matches every object (#329).
Matches when any child matches. Needs at least one child.
Matches when the child does not.
One test of one fact.

A reference to a reusable match fragment or application definition
in a library (#37), by ID and an optional version pin. A policy
document that is evaluated never holds one: the hierarchy replaces
every reference with the tree it names when it builds the effective
policy, and validation rejects one that is left (`unresolved_ref`).

Metadata.description:
Governance metadata (#40), on a policy, a rule set or a rule. Every
field is optional. Metadata is not decision-relevant: it never changes
what a rule decides ([`PolicyDocument::decision_relevant`]).

approved_by.description: Who approved it. Required for exception rules in governance mode.

compensating_controls.description: The controls that make up for the risk.

exception.description:
Mark the rule as an exception, in addition to the rules that are
exceptions by their nature ([`crate::lifecycle::is_exception`]).

justification.description:
Why the object exists. Required in governance mode for allow, trust,
exclusion and exception rules.

owner.description:
The principal who owns the object, such as a user or group ID. The
owner or a tenant administrator may edit it, and is notified before
it expires (#16).

review_by.description:
When it is due for review. Unset on an allow or trust rule means a
year after `created_at` ([`crate::lifecycle::review_by`]).

risk_rating.description: The risk it carries. Required for exception rules in governance mode.

tags.description: Free-form labels, each 1 to 128 characters, at most 64.

Mode.description:
How a policy's decisions take effect (#36).

The variants are declared from weakest to strongest, so the derived
ordering ranks them. The "strictest" merge in #36 treats `learning` and
`audit` as equally strong; that rule belongs to the merge code, not to this
ordering.

oneOf.description: The engine is not consulted. The device is reported as unprotected.
Evaluate fully, allow everything, and report would-block decisions.
Like `monitor`, with a full event for every decision.
Audit, and report every would-block object as a learning candidate.
Decisions take effect: blocked means blocked.

ModeOptions.description: Mode settings besides the base `mode`. Each is optional in a document.

disconnected_after_secs.description:
How long after its last successful check-in a device counts as
disconnected, in seconds: 60 to 2592000, and at least the check-in
interval. Unset means three check-in intervals.

mode_by_type.description:
The mode per object type, replacing the base mode for that type:
for example `script.powershell: audit` while everything else is
enforced. `disabled` is not allowed here: only a whole device can
be disabled.

mode_disconnected.description:
The base mode while the device is disconnected: `mode` itself or a
stricter mode, so losing the server never relaxes a device. It also
raises a weaker `mode_by_type`. Unset means the same as `mode`.

NetworkRef.description:
A network location test (#38). Address tests match when any local
interface address does.

oneOf.description: An address block, such as `10.20.0.0/16` or `2001:db8::/32`.
An inclusive address range, such as `10.0.0.10-10.0.0.99`.

A connection-specific DNS suffix, such as `corp.example.org`. Also
matches suffixes below it. Case-insensitive.
A default gateway's hardware address, such as `00-1a-2b-3c-4d-5e`.
Whether the management server is reachable.
A named location profile of the policy (`location_profiles`).

A network set from the library (#37): address blocks, ranges and DNS
suffixes.

Notify.description: Whether the user is shown a notification (#11).

oneOf.description: No notification.
The policy's default notification.
The rule's `notification_text`.

ObjectType.description: The class of object being evaluated. Scripts are `script.<kind>`.

OnExpire.description: What happens when a rule expires.

oneOf.description: The rule behaves as absent. The default.

The rule is deleted this many days after it expires (1 to 3650):
it behaves as absent at once, and [`crate::lifecycle::retire_due`]
lists it for deletion once the days have passed.

The rule becomes an `audit` rule: it still records matches, but no
longer decides.

OnWindowClose.description:
What happens to processes a scheduled allow let run, when its schedule
closes. The engine sends a directive; the agent and the tray act on it
(#4, #11).

oneOf.description: Nothing: they keep running. The default.
Warn the user.
Warn the user, then terminate them after the grace period.

Operator.description:
How a criterion compares the fact with its values (#32). Positive
operators match if any value matches; negative operators (`not_*`)
match if no value does, and never match a fact that is unknown.

oneOf.description: Equal to any value.
Equal to none of the values.

Starts with any value. On paths, the value must end at a component
boundary: `C:\Tools` does not match `C:\ToolsX`.
Ends with any value.
Contains any value.
Contains none of the values.
Matches any wildcard pattern.
Matches none of the wildcard patterns.

Matches any regular expression. Anchored at both ends, and run by a
linear-time engine without look-around or backreferences.
Matches none of the regular expressions.
Version equal to any value.
Version greater than the value.
Version greater than or equal to the value.
Version less than the value.
Version less than or equal to the value.

Version within `[min, max]`, both inclusive. Takes exactly two
values, the minimum first.
The set holds any of the values (#33).
The set holds none of the values (#33).
The fact is true. Takes no values (#33).

The fact is false. Takes no values (#33). On an unknown fact it is
unknown, like every other test.
Number, level or date equal to any value (#32).
Number, level or date equal to none of the values (#32).
Greater than the value (#32).
Greater than or equal to the value (#32).
Less than the value (#32).
Less than or equal to the value (#32).

Within `[min, max]`, both inclusive. Takes exactly two values, the
minimum first (#32).

The address is in any of the CIDR blocks, such as `10.0.0.0/8` or
`2001:db8::/32` (#32). On a set of addresses, any address may be.

The address is in any of the ranges, written `first-last` or, for
IPv4, `a.b.c.first-last` (#32).

The IPv4 address matches any whole-octet pattern, such as `10.*.*.*`
(#32).

The set holds at least one of the values (#32). The same test as
`member_of`.
The set holds every one of the values (#32).
The day of the week is any of the values, `mon` to `sun` (#32).

The time of day is within `[start, end)`, both `HH:MM`. A window
whose end is before its start wraps midnight: `22:00` to `06:00`
(#32).

The date is within `[from, to]`, both `YYYY-MM-DD` and inclusive
(#32).
What the criterion's `target` names exists (#329). Takes no values.

What the criterion's `target` names does not exist (#329). Takes no
values. Unknown when the agent did not look, like every negation.

Os.description:
The operating system a rule set targets. Other systems are reserved and
will be added in a minor version.

oneOf.description: Windows.

dn.description: The OU's distinguished name, such as `OU=Finance,DC=corp,DC=example`.

include_sub_ous.description: Also match devices in OUs below it.

Pin.description: `latest` (the newest version) or one version number.

Policy.description: The decision part of a policy: which rule sets apply, and how.

confirm_permit_all.description:
The confirmation a catch-all rule that lets objects run needs
(#35, #329): exactly [`CONFIRM_PERMIT_ALL`]. Without it, such a rule
is rejected (`permit_all_unconfirmed`).

governance.description:
Governance settings: justification, review and expiry rules, the
policy assistant's severities and counter reporting (#40).

id.description: Stable ID. Renaming the policy never changes it.

location_profiles.description:
Named network locations that scopes test with `location_profile`
(#38).

mode.description:
The base enforcement mode (#36). `disabled` is not allowed: only a
device can be disabled, with a reason and an expiry.

mode_options.description: The modes per object type and while disconnected (#36).

name.description:
Display name: 1 to 128 characters, trimmed, no control characters.
Uniqueness within a tenant is checked by the server (#10).

precedence_model.description: How matching rules are combined (#35, ADR 0004).

precedence_options.description:
Settings of the precedence models (#35). An option the selected
model does not use is ignored, with a warning.

revision.description: Monotonic revision, raised by the server on every change (#10).

rule_set_scopes.description:
The scopes of rule set assignments (#38): each rule of the set must
also be in every one of them. At most one entry per rule set.

rule_sets.description: The rule sets that apply, in order, by ID.

scope.description:
Who, where and when the whole policy applies (#38). Every rule must
also be in this scope.

settings.description: Typed settings. Every field has a documented default.

unknown.description:
What happens when no rule decides (#39). The default blocks every
unknown object.

PolicyId.description: The stable ID of a policy.

PolicySettings.description:
Settings that apply to the whole policy. Every field is optional in a
document and has the default shown in the schema.

advanced.description:
Engineering settings, checked against a registry of known keys. The
registry is empty in this version, so any key is rejected unless
`allow_unknown_advanced` is set. Keys are added only with the feature
that reads them (#330), and never relax a decision.

allow_unknown_advanced.description: Accept keys in `advanced` that the registry does not know.

capture_command_line.description:
Whether the agent records process command lines. Off by default for
privacy (#18).

condition_budget_ms.description:
The most time, in milliseconds, the agent spends collecting the
warm and cold facts of one rule (#33, #329): 1 to 10000, default
50. A fact not collected in time is unknown, with the trace note
`condition_timeout`. Separate from the per-decision watchdog (#42).

decision_cache_ttl_secs.description: How long a decision may be cached, in seconds. `0` disables the cache.

group_cache_max_age_secs.description:
How old cached group memberships that are not in the token
(cloud-directory groups) may be before scopes treat them as unknown,
in seconds (#38). From 3600 to 86400.

max_ancestor_depth.description: How many ancestors process criteria may inspect (#31).

max_criteria_per_rule.description:
Most criteria in one rule's match tree (#33): 1 to 32, the fixed
maximum and the default. A policy can tighten the limit, never
raise it.

max_tree_depth.description:
Deepest match tree (#33), where a single criterion has depth 1: 1 to
8, the fixed maximum and the default.

max_values_per_criterion.description:
Most values in one criterion (#33): 1 to 25, the fixed maximum and
the default.

override_durations.description:
Durations, in minutes, offered for override sessions (#9). At most 5
slots, each at most 10080. `0` marks a disabled slot.

script_control.description: Control level for scripts of a kind not listed in `script_control_by_kind`.

script_control_by_kind.description: Control level per script kind, overriding `script_control`.

time_zone_basis.description: Which clock schedules use, unless a schedule sets its own (#38).

PrecedenceModel.description:
How the matching rules of the ordinary rule sets are combined (#35).

The mandatory-deny tier and the implicit deny for unmatched files apply
under every model (ADR 0004). The semantics of each model are in
[`crate::precedence`].

oneOf.description: Any matching deny blocks; otherwise any matching allow allows. The default.
Any matching allow allows. Not recommended for Essential Eight.
The rule with the most specific identity wins.
Rules are ordered, and the first match decides.
The rule with the winning numeric priority decides.

PrecedenceOptions.description: Settings of the precedence models. Each is optional in a document.

allow_tiebreak.description:
Which allow decides when several allow rules of different kinds
could (`deny_wins`, `allow_wins` and `specificity`). The default,
`most_restrictive`, ranks `allow_contained` over `allow` over
`allow_elevated`.

curated_first.description:
`first_match` only: rules of curated (read-only) rule sets are
evaluated before every custom rule, whatever their `order`. On by
default.

granularity_tiebreak.description:
`allow_wins` only: within one rule set, a rule with a more specific
identity beats a less specific one before allow-over-deny applies,
so a denied file in an allowed folder stays denied. Off by default.

priority_direction.description:
`priority` only: whether the lowest or the highest `priority`
number wins. `lower_wins` by default.

same_tier_tiebreak.description:
`specificity` only: which action wins between rules of the same
specificity. `deny` by default.

PreexistingPolicy.description:
What happens to files that were on the device when the agent was
installed (origin `preexisting`).

oneOf.description: They are unknown like any other object.

The agent approves each one locally at install (#69). The engine
then sees the approvals as rules, and treats a file without one as
unknown.

They run only if the approved baseline (#5) allows them: at stage 6
they are blocked, whatever the levels say. The default.

PrincipalRef.description: A user or group (#38). Each is an object with one key, the kind.

oneOf.description: A user or group SID, such as `S-1-5-32-544`.
A well-known account or group.
A local group, by name, resolved on the device. Case-insensitive.
A directory group, by SID. The name is for display only.
A cloud-directory group, by tenant and object ID.

A wildcard on the `DOMAIN\user` account name, such as `*\svc_*`.
Names can be spoofed, so a pattern may only narrow a rule that lets
an object run, and only widen a deny (validation).
A principal set from the library (#37): SIDs and object IDs.
The lowest number wins. The default.
The highest number wins.

PromptOption.description: An answer the user may give to a prompt.

oneOf.description: Run this once.

Run it, and approve its hash on this device
([`crate::unknown::LocalApproval`]). The approval is uploaded for
review, and is temporary for objects from the internet, removable
media or a network.
Do not run it, and ask an administrator to approve it (#11).
Do not run it.

PromptSettings.description: How the `prompt` level asks the user.

fallback.description:
The level applied when the prompt times out, when there is no
interactive session, and for objects that cannot be prompted for.
Any level but `prompt`; the default is `block`.

options.description:
The answers offered, each at most once. The default is
`allow_once`, `request_approval` and `block`.

reauth.description: What the user must do again before an answer counts.

require_justification.description: The user must give a reason before an answer counts.

temp_approval_days.description:
How long an `allow_always_local` approval lasts, in days, for an
object from the internet, removable media or a network, or of
unknown origin: 1 to 90, default 14. Other approvals do not expire.

timeout_secs.description: How long the prompt waits, in seconds: 10 to 600, default 60.

Reauth.description:
What the user must do before an answer counts. Ordered from the
weakest to the strongest.

oneOf.description: Nothing more.
Enter their password again.
Complete multi-factor authentication.

RefList.description:
An `include` and an `exclude` list. An empty `include` means every
entry; a match in `exclude` always wins.

exclude.description: Never matches when any entry matches, whatever `include` says.

include.description: Matches when any entry matches. Empty means everyone or everything.

RefList2.description:
An `include` and an `exclude` list. An empty `include` means every
entry; a match in `exclude` always wins.

exclude.description: Never matches when any entry matches, whatever `include` says.

include.description: Matches when any entry matches. Empty means everyone or everything.

RefList3.description:
An `include` and an `exclude` list. An empty `include` means every
entry; a match in `exclude` always wins.

exclude.description: Never matches when any entry matches, whatever `include` says.

include.description: Matches when any entry matches. Empty means everyone or everything.

RequestTemplateRef.description: The ID of an approval request template (#11).

oneOf.description: Low.
Medium.
High.

Rule.description: One rule: a match tree and the action taken when it matches.

activates_at.description: The rule is absent before this instant (#40).

attribute.description:
A post-allow attribute rule (#33, #35, #329): stage 5. It is
evaluated only for an object stage 4 allowed, and only narrows that:
a `deny` blocks the object, and an `audit` annotates it. It needs no
identity anchor, because it can only take away an allow, such as
"PowerShell is allowed, but not with an encoded command". Only
`deny` and `audit`, never in a mandatory rule set, never a
catch-all. Unset means `false`.

catch_all.description:
A catch-all rule (#33, #35, #329): the default of its rule set, which
decides only when no other rule of stage 4 matched, under every
precedence model. It is the only rule that may have no identity
anchor, and the only one whose `match` may be an empty `all`, which
matches every object. At most one per rule set; its name starts
with `Default` or contains `Catch-all`; it allows, denies or audits;
and it is never in a mandatory rule set. Unset means `false`.

display_id.description: Human short ID from the tenant's sequence, `R-` and 6 to 12 digits.

effects.description:
Logging, upload, notification, severity and tags (#34). Unset
fields take the action's defaults.

enabled.description: Disabled rules are kept, but never decide.

enforcement_override.description: Per-rule enforcement override (#36). Only for `deny` rules.

expires_at.description:
The rule is absent from this instant on (#40). An expired allow
never revives, even if the clock is set back
([`crate::lifecycle`]).

name.description: Display name, with the same rules as a policy name.

object_types.description: The object classes the rule applies to. Empty means every class.

on_expire.description: What happens when the rule expires (#40).

order.description:
Position for the `first_match` model (#35): 0 to 1000000, lowest
first. Rules of custom (not read-only) rule sets use 100001 to
999989; the other ranges are reserved for system, curated and
catch-all rules.

scope.description:
Who, where and when the rule applies (#38). Unset means everyone,
everywhere, always, within the policy's and the rule set's scopes.

RuleId.description: The stable ID of a rule. It is never reused, even after the rule is deleted.

RuleSet.description: A named, reusable, ordered collection of rules.

allow_child_suppress.description:
Whether a group below the one that assigns this rule set may disable
one of its rules with `suppress_inherited` (#37). Unset means `true`
for an allowlist or a baseline and `false` for every other kind. A
mandatory rule set can never be suppressed (`suppress_not_allowed`).

band.description:
The `first_match` band of the hierarchy level that assigned this rule
set (#37): rules of a lower band come first, whatever their `order`.
The hierarchy writes it into an effective policy and replaces any
value an authored policy gives, so a local administrator cannot move
a rule set ahead of global policy. 0, the default, outside a
hierarchy.

category_path.description:
The category, as `Category` or `Category/Subcategory`: each part 1 to
64 characters, trimmed, with no `/` or control characters. Assigning
a category assigns every rule set library in it (#37).

kind.description: What the rule set is for.

mandatory.description:
Only for `blocklist`: evaluated in the non-overridable mandatory-deny
tier (#35, ADR 0004).

mode_override.description:
Only for a blocklist that is not mandatory: the mode its rules
decide in, replacing the mode for the object's type, for example to
try a new blocklist in `audit` (#36). `disabled` is not allowed.

name.description: Display name, with the same rules as a policy name.

os.description: The operating system the rules are written for.

read_only.description: Curated sets are read-only: edit a duplicate instead.

version.description: The content version of this rule set, for display (for example `3.0`).

RuleSetId.description: The stable ID of a rule set.

RuleSetKind.description: The purpose of a rule set.

oneOf.description: Rules that allow.
Rules that deny.
A baseline of what was present at a point in time.
Trusted sources (#9).
Elevation rules (#12).
Containment rules (#14).
Any mix of actions.

RuleSetScope.description:
The scopes of one rule-set assignment: every one must match for the
set's rules to apply.

rule_set.description: The rule set, which the policy must reference.

scopes.description:
From 1 to 8 scopes, all of which must match. In an effective policy
(#37) the contributing policy's own scope is added, so up to 9.

oneOf.description: Written by an administrator.
From learning mode (#5).
Accepted from a recommendation (#5).
From the curated catalogue.
Imported from another format.
Created through the API (#15).
From an approved user request (#11).

Schedule.description:
When a scope is active (#38).

Times are wall-clock times in the schedule's time zone. A window starts
on one of its days at `start` and lasts until `end` (which may be on
the next day: `22:00` to `06:00` wraps midnight) or for `duration_mins`.
With no windows, every time of day is in. `dates` and `except_dates`
test the local date of the moment being decided.

dates.description: Absolute date ranges. Empty means every date.

except_dates.description: Dates on which the schedule is never active, such as holidays.

grace_secs.description:
Seconds between the warning and termination, for
`warn_then_terminate`. Default 300.

on_window_close.description:
Only for rules that let an object run: what happens to running
processes when the schedule closes.

timezone_basis.description:
The clock the times are read on. Unset means the policy's
`settings.time_zone_basis`.

windows.description: The weekly windows. Empty means all day, every day.

SchemaVersion.description: A semantic version MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, without pre-release or build suffixes.

Scope.description:
Who, where and when a rule applies (#38).

Every field is optional. An empty scope applies to everyone, everywhere,
always. A scope only ever narrows: a rule applies when its match tree
matches **and** every scope on the way to it matches (the policy's, its
rule set assignment's, and its own).

combine.description:
How the dimensions that are set combine: `all` (the default) needs
every one to match, `any` needs one.

max_instances_per_session.description:
Only on the scope of a rule that lets an object run: at most this
many instances per session. `0`, the default, means no limit.

negate.description: Apply when the scope does **not** match.

schedule.description:
When the scope is active, written in place. At most one of
`schedule` and `schedule_set`.

schedule_set.description: When the scope is active, as a schedule from the library (#37).

sessions.description: The session type and, on a multi-session host, the connecting client.

ScopeLimit.description:
One contributing policy's limit on where its unknown settings apply, in
an effective policy ([`UnknownPolicy::scope_limits`]). It holds when
every scope of `all_of` matches and, if `any_of` is not empty, one of
its scopes matches.

all_of.description:
The contributing policy's `policy.scope`, if it has one. At most one
scope: the width of an entry is never more than its source policy's,
so the authored limits apply to it unchanged.

ScopeSubject.description: Whose token a scope's `principals` is tested against.

oneOf.description: The user the process runs as. The default.

The user logged on to the process's session, for example to scope a
service running as SYSTEM on behalf of the interactive user.
The user the parent process runs as.

client.description: The connecting client, on a multi-session host.

types.description: The session types. Empty means every type.

oneOf.description: The physical console.
A remote desktop session.
A remote shell, such as a remote PowerShell session.
A service.
A batch job, such as a scheduled task.
A network logon.

SignerOptions.description:
The options of a signer criterion (#31).

A signer criterion matches if any signature that takes part satisfies
it. A signature takes part when its status is accepted, it comes from
the chosen source and has the chosen index, and it meets every
constraint here (`signed_after`, `countersigned`, `min_key_bits` and
`disallowed_algorithms`). A constraint whose fact is unknown makes that
signature's result unknown, never a match.

accept_status.description:
The signature statuses that can match. Unset means `valid`,
`valid_expired_timestamped` and `catalog_signed`. `digest_mismatch`
cannot be listed: see `allow_digest_mismatch`. Validation warns when
a rule that lets an object run accepts any other status.

allow_digest_mismatch.description:
Let a signature whose signed digest does not match the file take
part: the file was changed after it was signed. Validation always
warns about it. Unset means `false`.

component.description:
Only for `signer.publisher`: the part of the leaf subject compared.
Unset means `cn`.

countersigned.description:
The signature must carry an RFC 3161 timestamp that verifies.
Unset means `false`: no requirement.

disallowed_algorithms.description:
The signature must use none of these digest algorithms, in the
file digest, the signer information or any certificate of its chain.

min_key_bits.description:
Every key in the signature's chain must be at least this strong, in
RSA-equivalent bits (see [`crate::facts::KeyFact::rsa_equivalent_bits`]).

position.description:
Only for `signer.tbs_hash` and `signer.spki_sha256`: where in the
chain the certificate must be. Unset means `any`.

signature_index.description:
Only the signature at this index, counted from 0 among the
signatures of `source`: 0 is the primary embedded signature, 1 the
first nested one. Unset means any signature.

signed_after.description:
A trusted timestamp must show that the signature was made at or
after this instant: an RFC 3339 time with an offset, such as
`2024-01-01T00:00:00Z`. A signature with no trusted timestamp is
unknown.

source.description: Where the signature must come from. Unset means `any`.

SignerSource.description: Where the signatures a signer criterion looks at come from (#31).

oneOf.description: Embedded in the file.
A signed catalog that lists the file's hash.
Either.

SignerStatus.description:
The result of verifying one signature (#31, #48). An unsigned object
has no [`SignerFact`] at all.

oneOf.description: The signature and chain verify, and the certificate is in date.

The certificate has expired, but a trusted timestamp shows that the
signature was made while it was valid.
The signature verifies through a signed catalog.
The certificate has expired, with no trusted timestamp.
The certificate has been revoked.
The chain ends at a root that is not trusted.
The file's content does not match the signed digest.

SubjectComponent.description:
The part of the leaf certificate's subject that `signer.publisher`
compares (#31).

oneOf.description: The common name.
The organisation.
The whole distinguished name, as RFC 4514 writes it.

TbsPosition.description:
Where the certificate of a `signer.tbs_hash` or `signer.spki_sha256`
test must be (#31, #318).

oneOf.description: The leaf: the certificate that signed.
Any certificate between the leaf and the root.
The root of the chain.
Anywhere in the chain.

TierTiebreak.description: Which action wins between rules of the same specificity.

oneOf.description: A deny beats an allow. The default.
An allow beats a deny.

TimeZoneBasis.description: The clock that schedules are interpreted in.

oneOf.description: The device's local time zone.
Coordinated Universal Time.

The time zone of the session's user, if the agent can read it, and
otherwise the device's (#38).

Timestamp.description: An RFC 3339 date-time, such as `2026-11-25T09:30:00Z`. Read as UTC; fractions of a second are dropped.

TokenProfileRef.description: The ID of an access token profile for elevation (#12, #150).

TrustMode.description: How far trust from a `trust_source` action reaches (#114).

oneOf.description: Only files the designated process writes itself.
Files the designated process and all its descendants write.

UnknownAs.description: How a deny rule treats a result it cannot decide (#32, #35).

oneOf.description: The rule does not apply. The default.
The rule applies, so the deny blocks.

UnknownPolicy.description:
The unknown-application policy (#39). Every field is optional in a
document; the defaults block every unknown object.

allow_request.description: When an unknown object is blocked, the user may ask for approval (#11).

by_type.description:
The level per object type. `restrict` only for executables, scripts
and installers; `prompt` not for libraries or drivers.

default.description: The level when no entry below applies. The default is `block`.

driver_boot_policy.description: How unknown drivers are handled during early boot.

effects.description:
Logging, upload, notification, severity and tags of unknown-object
decisions (#34). `log` must be `always` or `sampled`: an unhandled
object is always reported.

preexisting_policy.description: What happens to files present at install.

preset.description: The compliance preset this policy started from, if any.

restrict_profile.description:
The containment profile of the `restrict` level (#14). Required when
any level, or the prompt's fallback, is `restrict`.

scope_limits.description:
Effective policies only (#37): where these settings apply, one
[`ScopeLimit`] per contributing policy, kept as that policy wrote it.
The settings apply to a subject when **any** entry holds; empty, the
default, means no further limit. An effective policy has no
`policy.scope`, so the hierarchy moves each contributing policy's
`scope` and `scopes` here unexpanded
([`UnknownPolicy::scope_limit_of`]). The size is therefore linear in
contributing policies, at most `MAX_CONTRIBUTING_POLICIES` (in
`hierarchy::limits`) entries, and building an effective policy from valid policies never
fails on it. Validation rejects it in a document it validates as
authored, which writes `policy.scope` and `unknown.scopes` instead.

scopes.description:
Where these settings apply, besides the policy's `scope` (#38): a
subject in at least one of these scopes, at most 1000. Empty, the
default, means wherever the policy applies. A subject outside it is
decided by the built-in implicit deny ([`crate::unknown`]).

Upload.description: When an event is sent to the server.

oneOf.description: As soon as possible.
With the next batch.
Never: kept in the local log only.

UtcDate.description: An RFC 3339 full date, such as `2026-11-25`, in UTC.

Uuid7.description: A UUID version 7 in canonical lowercase form.

oneOf.description: Monday.
Tuesday.
Wednesday.
Thursday.
Friday.
Saturday.
Sunday.

WellKnown.description: A well-known account or group, with a fixed SID.

oneOf.description: The local Administrators group, `S-1-5-32-544`.
The local Users group, `S-1-5-32-545`.
The local system account, `S-1-5-18`.
Interactive logons, `S-1-5-4`.

Any domain's Domain Controllers group (relative ID 516), or the
Enterprise Domain Controllers group, `S-1-5-9`.

days.description: The days the window starts on. At least one, each once.

duration_mins.description: How long it lasts, in minutes, from 1 to 10080.

end.description:
When it ends, `HH:MM`. At or before `start` means the next day.
Exactly one of `end` and `duration_mins`.

description: A versioned policy document: one policy and the rule sets it uses.

rule_sets.description:
The rule sets the policy references, in any order. The policy's
`rule_sets` list gives the order that applies.

schema_version.description:
The version of this schema the document was written for. A reader
accepts the same major version and any minor version.

title: Palisade policy document
